messages:
Maria (Support): customer reported that batch rerank is returning scores that don't line up with per-query candidate lists. report attached, high priority. 
Kevin (Eng): can you paste the raw request + response (redact keys) and the request_id?
Maria (Support): request_id=rb-2026-03-15-89fa. here's the sanitized payload we used: 
```json
{
  \"model\": \"rerank-v1\",
  \"queries\": [\"find best running shoes\", \"top noise-cancelling headphones\"],
  \"candidate_lists\": [
    [\"shoeA\", \"shoeB\", \"shoeC\"],
    [\"headphoneX\", \"headphoneY\"]
  ],
  \"per_query\": true
}
```
and the service returned: 
```json
{
  \"scores\": [0.92, 0.51, 0.38, 0.67, 0.45],
  \"metadata\": {\"note\": \"flattened scores - ambiguous mapping\"}
}
```
The problem: we expected scores to map 3->2 but the user saw pairs: shoeA->0.92, shoeB->0.51, shoeC->0.38, headphoneX->0.67, headphoneY->0.45 which is correct ordering, but for another customer the mapping was shifted (e.g. headphoneX got shoeC score). They see intermittent misalignment in prod for multi-query batches when candidate counts vary.
Anika (SRE): do we have logs that show candidate_count vs score_count per request_id? can we reproduce locally by sending same shape?
Maria (Support): I repro'd locally with a simplified curl and saw the shift. Putting the repro snippet below. Repro is intermittent — about 1/50 requests when run in a tight loop.
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '@payload.json' | jq . > out$i.json
done
```
payload.json is the JSON above. After running, compare lengths and check mapping: we saw out37.json where counts matched but mapping appeared shifted by one for the second query.
Kevin (Eng): ok thanks. two hypotheses: 1) request-level flattening bug where internal batching flattens candidate_lists and uses a global offset table but a race causes offsets to be computed per-batch instead of per-request; 2) an optimization in the rerank runtime that merges KV cache entries across concurrent subrequests and then reconstructs score arrays using stale offsets.
Sam (Oncall): tagging @rerank-bot to surface matching deploys around the request time.
rerank-bot: deploy-event detected: rerank-service v2.14.3 deployed 2026-03-15T08:32:10Z to prod (canary->stable).
Anika (SRE): that deploy timestamp lines up with the first customer report. Kevin, can you try to reproduce against the canary or a staging build pinned to v2.14.2 vs v2.14.3?
Kevin (Eng): yes. I ran stress tests against both. v2.14.2 shows 0/1000 failures. v2.14.3 shows ~6/1000 repros with the exact shift pattern Maria described. I captured wire logs for one failing request — internal log shows: 
```
[2026-03-15T08:45:12Z] request rb-2026-03-15-89fa received: queries=2 total_candidates=5
[2026-03-15T08:45:12Z] flattening candidate lists -> flat_indexing start_offsets=[0,3] total=5
[2026-03-15T08:45:12Z] batched infer started for batch_id=8243
[2026-03-15T08:45:12Z] compute_offsets based on in-flight batch (race) -> start_offsets=[0,2]  <-- incorrect
[2026-03-15T08:45:12Z] scores computed: [0.92,0.51,0.38,0.67,0.45]
[2026-03-15T08:45:12Z] remap scores to per-query slices using start_offsets=[0,2] -> query0=[0.92,0.51], query1=[0.38,0.67,0.45]  <-- shifted
```
Kevin (Eng): that log looks like a race when computing start_offsets for flattened candidate arrays when multiple requests are multiplexed into a single GPU batch. the start_offsets were computed from in-flight batch metadata instead of the per-request candidate counts.
Maria (Support): customer impact: several customers have reported mismatched top-k picks in production; one customer disabled rerank and saw immediate fix. billing: no errors thrown, just bad labels, so SLAs unaffected but correctness is broken.
Anika (SRE): mitigation: rollback to v2.14.2 for router->rerank path or enable strict non-multiplexed batching for known-affected customers. rolling rollback will take ~20m.
Kevin (Eng): quick patch idea: compute and attach per-request start_offsets earlier (at ingress) and pass them through the batch bundle so remapping can't use global batch-derived offsets. low-risk change. I'll open a PR that pins offsets to the request proto and adds an assertion in remapper.
Sam (Oncall): action items: 1) Kevin to open PR + canary PR by EOD, 2) Anika to prepare rollback playbook if PR is unsafe, 3) Maria to notify affected customers with a short incident note and workaround (disable rerank or use single-query requests).
Maria (Support): I'll draft the customer note and message customers who reported it. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Kevin (Eng): creating PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/compare/bugfix/offsets-pin-1959
Anika (SRE): I'll start the rollback readiness checklist and verify metrics for canary traffic.
rerank-bot: incident ticket created #INC-4897.
Maria (Support): saved repro artifacts to \"/mnt/eng/repro/rb-2026-03-15-89fa/\" including out37.json and full wire logs.
Kevin (Eng): when PR lands we'll add a regression test that fuzzes candidate_list sizes and asserts remapped lengths match original per-query lengths.
Maria (Support): closing loop here — if any customer asks for ETA I'll point at this thread.
